subject: Q3 objectives handback + QBR checklist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 objectives handback + QBR checklist

Team — attaching the first-pass handback for Q3 objectives plus a compact QBR readiness checklist. This is the playbook I promised after the leadership sync last week. High-level notes up top, details and asks below.

Attachments: Q3_Objectives_v1.pdf (pdf), QBR_Checklist_v1.md (markdown)

Key context:
- We need explicit sign-off on the customer-facing objectives (Growth, Reliability, Cost Efficiency) by EOD Wed so CS/RevOps can finalize QoS and renewals messaging.
- Acme Analytics (copied) requested clarified SLO baselines and an operational mitigation plan for the first 30 days after launch.

Asks (please):
1) Vivek — confirm revenue target cadence and whether we want to break out dedicated vs hosted in the objectives. If yes, I put a draft split on page 2.
2) Aditya — confirm instrumentation milestone and evaluation harness timelines (I marked them green if we can get dev sign-off by 7/19).
3) Lauren — review the QBR checklist and add any CS/partner-specific evidence items we need for Acme.

I left a short list of risk mitigations on page 4 (traffic shaping, fallback policy, and a fast rollback checklist). If you want any of these pulled into a separate runbook I can draft that after sign-off.

Next steps: please reply in-thread with a single-line approve/reject + one-line rationale so we have a clean audit for the QBR packet. If we have open items, flag them and I will schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
--

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 objectives handback + QBR checklist

Soojin — quick pass notes inline:

- Pg1: Growth objective looks fine, but baseline seems to use May numbers; can we move to a trailing-90-day baseline (ends 7/1) so targets are tethered to actual trend?
- Pg2: I agree with splitting hosted vs dedicated. Suggest we frame dedicated as a capacity commitment metric (commits/mth) rather than raw revenue — easier for sales to pitch.
- Instrumentation: We cannot guarantee the eval harness by 7/19 unless we deprioritize a mid-cycle refactor. I marked it amber.

Approve in principle pending baseline update and instrumentation timeline clarity.

Aditya
Director, Growth & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 objectives handback + QBR checklist

Thanks — reading now and left a couple of comments in Drive. High level:

- Revenue target: tighten to reflect 12% QoQ growth vs the 18% on page 2. The 18% is aspirational but we need something we can defend in the board packet. I put proposed wording: "Target: 12% QoQ - defendable vs trailing 90-day TAM expansion rate."
- Dedicated vs hosted: keep the split but don’t publish the dedicated number in the customer-facing QBR packet; present it as an internal commitment metric in the appendix. That keeps contract negotiation clean.
- Risk mitigations: make traffic shaping mitigation explicit — require a 15-minute manual escalation window, then automated fallback.

Can we do a 30-min alignment at 3pm PT today to sign off? I can send a calendar invite. If any of you are not available, propose a slot tomorrow morning.

Approve in principle pending the two edits above (baseline and revenue).

Vivek
VP, Revenue & Strategy
Redwood Inference
